svg.title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Brokerage Desk
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Brokerage Desk; subtitle: Build execution readiness first; the first deal may take 1–3 months.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Milestones describe implementation work rather than promised sales. Use operator-owned accounts and authorized supplier inventory. Do not fund positions that fail rights, liquidity, pricing, or delivery checks.; caption: By day 30, produce a rights file, tested inventory controls, a priced offer set, and a cash-exposure report. Revenue and owner profit follow completed, reconciled transactions.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Map rights and settlement obligations; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one initial model, identify applicable reseller requirements, inspect supplier contracts, and document exchange payout terms. Build separate gross, retained revenue, expense, customer-deposit, and cash-reserve accounts.; label: Days 8-14; value: Test inventory and payment controls; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure the selected POS and supported channels. Test holds, stale-feed alerts, authorized transfers, duplicate order handling, and invoice matching using permitted test procedures. Record observed latency and a manual delisting procedure for failed synchronization.; label: Days 15-21; value: Underwrite offers and qualify buyers; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Price five small inventory-backed offers with acquisition, fees, markdown exposure, disruption provision, operations, and funding costs. Begin the corporate cohort ledger; collect deposits only against clear contracts and supportable delivery rights.; label: Days 22-30; value: Reconcile pilot or rehearse settlement; numeric value: 30.0; detail: If a legitimate pilot sale occurs, reconcile payment, transfer, and expected payout without declaring premature profit. Otherwise rehearse a cancellation and 30-day settlement delay. Schedule the next 60 days around the canonical 1–3 month first-deal window.

text.title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Brokerage Desk
text.tspan: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Brokerage Desk

rect.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Map rights and settlement obligations; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one initial model, identify applicable reseller requirements, inspect supplier contracts, and document exchange payout terms. Build separate gross, retained revenue, expense, customer-deposit, and cash-reserve accounts.

label: Days 8-14; value: Test inventory and payment controls; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure the selected POS and supported channels. Test holds, stale-feed alerts, authorized transfers, duplicate order handling, and invoice matching using permitted test procedures. Record observed latency and a manual delisting procedure for failed synchronization.

label: Days 15-21; value: Underwrite offers and qualify buyers; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Price five small inventory-backed offers with acquisition, fees, markdown exposure, disruption provision, operations, and funding costs. Begin the corporate cohort ledger; collect deposits only against clear contracts and supportable delivery rights.

label: Days 22-30; value: Reconcile pilot or rehearse settlement; numeric value: 30.0; detail: If a legitimate pilot sale occurs, reconcile payment, transfer, and expected payout without declaring premature profit. Otherwise rehearse a cancellation and 30-day settlement delay. Schedule the next 60 days around the canonical 1–3 month first-deal window.

text.title: Assumptions: Milestones describe implementation work rather than promised sales. Use operator-owned accounts and authorized supplier inventory. Do not fund positions that fail rights, liquidity, pricing, or delivery checks.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Milestones describe implementation work rather than promised sales. Use operator-owned accounts and authorized supplier
inventory. Do not fund positions that fail rights, liquidity, pricing, or delivery checks.
